newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire reinforces troops after Tutsi rebel clashes.
newsitem.headline: Zaire reinforces troops after Tutsi rebel clashes.

text.p: Zaire has been reinforcing and rearming its troops in its eastern refugee zone following fresh clashes with ethnic Tutsi rebels near the border with Burundi, residents and eyewitnesses say.
One U.N. source, who chose to remain anonymous, said trucks carrying reinforcements for Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels apparently crossed from Burundi before the latest clash on Friday.

No immediate death toll was available in the refugee town of Bukavu. But aid workers said earlier by telephone from the eastern Zaire town of Uvira that three people were killed and a number of Banyamulenge were taken prisoner on Friday.
They said that up to 26,400 mainly Burundi refugees from earlier fighting in their country had fled a camp near Uvira.
"I can confirm that Kagunga camp is now empty because of the fighting," said Fernando Del Mundo, spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR, said in Geneva.

Zaire is host to hundreds of thousands of Hutu refugees who fled fearing reprisals in Rwanda after the 1994 massacres of minority Tutsis by Hutu hardliners there or who fled ethnic conflict between Hutus and Tutsis in Burundi.

The Banyamulenge are ethnic Tutsis, some of whom have lived in Zaire for generations. Zaire accuses the Tutsi-dominated army of Rwanda of training and arming Banyamulenge guerrillas to destabilise the region.
"The fighting began very early this morning," Francoise Clement, head of the International Committee of the Red Cross delegation in Bukavu, 130 km (80 miles) north of Uvira, told Reuters.
Fighting took place near a sugar factory in the village of Kiliba about 15 km (10 miles) from Uvira, where aid workers reported numerous wounded arriving during the afternoon.
A Red Cross transport plane carrying doctors to reinforce hospital care in the region turned back after being hit by bullets as it tried to land at Kiliba. It later landed at Goma.
The fighting was the second major round in Zaire in a week. Last Sunday about 20,000 Hutu refugees from Burundi fled their camp in eastern Zaire after it was attacked by armed men.
Four refugees were killed and six wounded in Runingo camp, a U.N. source said. Del Mundo said Runingo was also still empty.

A U.N. source said two trucks carrying young Zairean men had been sent to help troops in the area. "There were 30 trucks carrying the rebels to Kiliba. It appears they came from the other side of the Burundian border," the source added.
Missionary workers in the area said the rebels withdrew to a plateau where the Banyamulenge had a stronghold above Uvira.

Bukavu residents report large numbers of extra Zairean troops arriving in the area over the past few days. One witness said several plane loads of weapons, including Katyusha rocket launchers, had arrived in Bukavu over the past three days.
Zaire military units in Bukavu on Friday told businesses in the town to lend them trucks for "the security of the town".
An army document ordered traders to provide a truck, driver and 20 litres of gasoline to the army for one day a week.
Earlier, witnesses said troops destroyed a bridge on the road from Uvira to Bukavu and turned back trucks heading south.
Bukavu residents, who say some Zairean soldiers demand protection money from businesses, fear unpaid or ill-disciplined Zairean troops may turn to looting if things go wrong.
